name: M0 — Mobile status audit document (current state of mobile mode)
description:
OBJECTIVE
Produce the written audit of the CURRENT mobile mode of the codx-junior web client (Vue 3 + Vuex + vue-router + daisyUI/Tailwind + dockview). It is the baseline document for the whole "Mobile Refactor" board: it must let a non-technical reader understand the problem and give the developers a precise inventory of modules, routes and defects.

OUTPUT FILE
docs/mobile/mobile-current-status.md (create folder if missing). Single markdown document, Spanish/English as used in repo comments (English preferred). Keep it stable in structure so later updates can be diffed.

REQUIRED CONTENT
1. Executive summary (max 10 lines): what breaks on a phone today, business impact, and the 3 root causes.
2. Module & route inventory table: for EVERY app/module list — appKey, visible title, route name + path, resolved component, desktop mode (panel?) vs single mode (route?), and mobile status (OK / degrades / broken / unknown). Build it from these three files and flag ANY mismatch between them (a key in config/apps.js without a registered route, a route whose component is missing, etc.):
   - src/config/apps.js (APPS registry — single source of truth for "how to open an app")
   - src/router/index.ts (project-scoped routes, /:projectName/...)
   - src/config/appComponentsMap.js (appKey -> lazy component)
3. Navigation model as it exists today: route-derived mode (isDesktopMode() === route name 'codx-junior-split'), config/apps.js + router/navigate.js openApp(), AppRouteView.vue resolution, and the payload hand-off setPendingParams/getPendingParams.
4. Shell audit: src/App.vue (what chrome exists on mobile), src/components/desktop/DesktopSidebar.vue (rail + overlay in one component), src/components/desktop/Desktop.vue, src/main.ts.
5. Per-screen consistency audit: pick the 10 heaviest screens (ChatView/Chat, KanbanBoardView, GlobalSettings, ProjectSettings, KnowledgeView, VibeCodingView, TeamView, InfraView, FileExplorerPanel, ManagementDashboardView) and record for each: does it render its own header? its own sidebar/drawer? its own scrolling container? does it work at 375 px? does it have a way back?
6. Defect list, each with file:line evidence, severity (blocker/high/medium/low) and a one-line fix direction. MUST include at least (verify each before writing):
   D1 Two conflicting definitions of "mobile": src/store/ui.js handleResize uses width <= 1024; src/App.vue uses window.innerWidth < 768; src/components/chat/ProfileDrawer.vue uses < 1024. Consequence in the 768–1024 band.
   D2 No visible global navigation: on mobile App.vue collapses the sidebar on every route change and the only expand controls live INSIDE the off-canvas panel (translateX(-100%)), so navigation is unreachable after the first navigation.
   D3 No mobile chrome at all: App.vue renders <RouterView/> with no app bar, no title, no back button, no bottom navigation; each screen invents its own.
   D4 Mode comes from the route, not the device: opening .../desktop on a phone mounts the dockview workspace.
   D5 Rich payloads travel in memory (setPendingParams): refresh / back-forward / shared link loses chat, team, channel, workspace, member → screens receive undefined.
   D6 src/components/ChatEntry.vue imports and renders ./ChatEntryMobile.vue, which DOES NOT EXIST in the repo (verify) → mobile message rendering is broken / build-blocking.
   D7 Orphan & legacy mobile code: src/components/mobile/MenuBar.vue (uses <ProjectSelector>, <Notifications>, <UserMenu> without importing them, referenced nowhere); views/HomeMobile.vue referenced by an older App.vue and absent; SplitView.vue/Splitter.vue no longer mounted by the router.
   D8 Registry bypass: legacy $ui.showApp({component}) call sites in src/store/ui.js (e.g. openMediaLibrary with field typos tgabId / compotabIdnent) do not go through config/apps.js, so they cannot work in route (mobile) mode.
   D9 No shared mobile primitives: no page header/back component, no bottom nav, no safe-area-inset handling, no scroll-lock, body{overflow:hidden} + h-full assumptions in index.html, inconsistent touch-target sizes.
7. Duplication map: components that exist twice for mobile/desktop or that duplicate content blocks (GlobalSettings desktop aside vs mobile drawer with 10 duplicated v-if branches, ChatEntry vs ChatEntryMobile, default.vue/built-in toolbars of each screen).
8. Constraints & risks for the refactor (dockview is desktop-only, deep links must keep working, per-project URL prefix, saved layouts in localStorage, eruda debug hook in main.ts).
9. Annex: proposed target principles (one navigation model, one page chrome component, one viewport source of truth) — 1 page max, no code.

RULES
- Read the files; do not trust this description blindly. Report any finding that no longer reproduces as "already fixed".
- No code changes. Documentation only. Cite file paths (and line numbers when useful) for every claim.
- Markdown tables, no screenshots required.

ACCEPTANCE
- docs/mobile/mobile-current-status.md exists, follows the 9 sections, every app from config/apps.js appears in the inventory, and each defect has file evidence + severity.
- Summary reply to the task lists: file path, number of modules inventoried, number of defects by severity, and the 3 root causes.
